blocks.content: 1. INTRODUCTION

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Metals are electropositive elements that lose electrons to form positive ions, while non-metals are electronegative elements that gain electrons.
Metals form basic or amphoteric oxides, whereas non-metals form acidic or neutral oxides.
Highly reactive metals like sodium and potassium are kept submerged in kerosene oil to prevent spontaneous combustion in air.
Ionic compounds formed between metals and non-metals possess high melting points and conduct electricity in molten or aqueous states.
Galvanisation protects iron from rusting by applying a protective coating of zinc.

blocks.content:
All the elements found in nature can be divided into two main categories known as metals and non-metals.

These elements are used by human beings in daily life for various purposes such as cooking, construction, transportation, electricity and medicine.

Metals and non-metals differ from each other in their physical properties, chemical properties and uses.

Understanding the difference between metals and non-metals is very important in chemistry.
2. METALS

Metals are those elements which are generally hard, shiny and strong in nature.

They are good conductors of heat and electricity and are widely used in industries and households.

Most metals exist in solid state at room temperature, but mercury is an exception because it exists in liquid state.

Metals play an important role in the development of civilization and modern technology.
2.1 PHYSICAL PROPERTIES OF METALS

Metals are lustrous in nature, which means they have a shining surface.

They are generally hard, although some metals like sodium and potassium are soft and can be cut with a knife.

Metals are malleable, which means they can be beaten into thin sheets without breaking.

Metals are ductile, which means they can be drawn into thin wires.

Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity, which is why copper and aluminium are used in electrical wires.

Metals are sonorous, which means they produce a ringing sound when struck with a hard object.
2.2 CHEMICAL PROPERTIES OF METALS

Metals react with oxygen to form metal oxides.

These metal oxides are generally basic in nature.

Some metals react with water to form metal hydroxides and hydrogen gas.

Metals also react with acids to form salts and hydrogen gas.

A more reactive metal can displace a less reactive metal from its compound in a chemical reaction.
3. NON‑METALS

Non-metals are elements which do not show the properties of metals.

They are generally dull in appearance and are poor conductors of heat and electricity.

Most non-metals are found in gaseous state, while some are solids.

Non-metals play an important role in life processes and industries.
Metals are electropositive elements that readily lose electrons to form cations, whereas non-metals gain electrons to form anions.
3.1 PHYSICAL PROPERTIES OF NON‑METALS

Non-metals are generally dull in appearance and do not shine.

They are not malleable, which means they cannot be beaten into thin sheets.

They are not ductile and cannot be drawn into wires.

Non-metals are poor conductors of heat and electricity.

Graphite is an exception because it conducts electricity.
3.2 CHEMICAL PROPERTIES OF NON‑METALS

Non-metals react with oxygen to form non-metal oxides.

These oxides are generally acidic in nature.

Non-metals do not react with acids to produce hydrogen gas.

Non-metals usually form covalent compounds by sharing electrons.
4. DIFFERENCE BETWEEN METALS AND NON‑METALS

rows: Do not react with water or steam

blocks.content:
Metals are shiny, whereas non-metals are generally dull in appearance.

Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity, whereas non-metals are poor conductors.

Metals are malleable and ductile, whereas non-metals are brittle.

Metals form basic oxides, whereas non-metals form acidic oxides.
5. REACTIVITY SERIES

The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in decreasing order of their reactivity.

Potassium is the most reactive metal, while gold is one of the least reactive metals.

The reactivity series helps in predicting displacement reactions.

It also helps in deciding the method used for extraction of metals from their ores.
6. CORROSION

Corrosion is the slow destruction of metals due to their reaction with air, moisture or chemicals.

The most common example of corrosion is rusting of iron.

Rusting occurs when iron reacts with oxygen and water to form hydrated iron oxide.

Corrosion weakens metals and causes great economic loss.
7. PREVENTION OF CORROSION

Corrosion can be prevented by various methods.

Painting the surface of metals prevents air and moisture from coming in contact with the metal.

Oiling and greasing are also used to prevent rusting.

Galvanization is a process in which iron is coated with a layer of zinc to prevent corrosion.

Electroplating is another method in which a protective metal layer is deposited using electricity.

Making alloys also helps in reducing corrosion.
8. USES OF METALS AND NON‑METALS

items: Aqua Regia is a freshly prepared 3:1 ratio mixture of concentrated Hydrochloric Acid (HCl) and concentrated Nitric Acid (HNO3).
Amphoteric oxides, such as Aluminium Oxide (Al2O3) and Zinc Oxide (ZnO), react with both acids and bases to yield salt and water.
Diamond is a non-metal allotrope with the highest thermal conductivity and hardness, while Graphite is a non-metal that conducts electricity.
Cinnabar (HgS) is the ore of mercury from which mercury is extracted simply by heating in air (roasting).

blocks.content:
Metals such as iron and steel are used in construction of buildings, bridges and machines.

Copper is used in electrical wiring because it is a good conductor of electricity.

Aluminium is used in making utensils and aircraft because it is light and strong.

Oxygen is a non-metal used for respiration.

Nitrogen is used in fertilizers to increase crop yield.

Carbon is used as fuel and in making pencils.
9. IMPORTANT EXAM POINTS

Mercury is the only metal that exists in liquid state.

Sodium and potassium are highly reactive metals.

Gold and silver are least reactive metals.

Rusting is a type of corrosion.

Non-metals generally form acidic oxides.
10. QUICK REVISION

Metals are shiny, malleable and good conductors of electricity.

Non-metals are dull and poor conductors.

Reactivity series shows the order of reactivity of metals.

Corrosion damages metals and can be prevented.

Metals and non-metals are very important in daily life.
